errors.english: speaks according to the ways of a superior person
errors.why: skyes bu'i lugs (Skt. puruṣālāpa) means the peacock speaks in human fashion, i.e. has human speech, not that he speaks like a superior person.

note: A faithful rendering of the Tibetan verses of the queen's poisoning scheme; only the peacock's human speech is blurred.

errors.english: literally "an act that is not un-blameworthy,"
errors.why: kha na ma tho ba renders avadya, simply 'fault, blameworthy deed'; the double-negative gloss is wrong.

fix.find: literally "an act that is not un-blameworthy,"

note: Sound rendering of the Vinaya theft casuistry (owner types, robbery from a thief, pārājika) with one misleading note.

errors.english: release the final knot of the lower robe
errors.why: dor ba here likely means to tie/fasten: the monk should knot the end of the lower robe when climbing a ladder or sleeping by day, which is why the stated purpose is keeping the private parts covered.

note: Verse and commentary on barbering and deportment are well segmented and largely accurate; the robe-knot rule is probably inverted.
Faithful rendering of the argument that mind, not body, is the cause of mind, with verses and the fire-and-wood objection correctly handled.
Accurate commentary on proxy consent (chanda) and on a monk detained on the poṣadha day; the procedure is followed step by step.

errors.why: 'char ba and nub pa here (cf. the previous side) are rising and setting, as of the sun in the stock inference example, not arising and ceasing of things in general.

errors.english: The author uses the analogy of a mortar and pestle
errors.why: Nothing in the side supports a mortar-and-pestle analogy; the note is a guess built on an uncertain reading of a lemma.

errors.english: of the nature of perceiving a pervading contradiction
errors.why: This is the reason-type viruddhavyāptopalabdhi, 'apprehension of something pervaded by what is contradictory', and the passage explains an example of a thesis invalidated by pramāṇa, not a 'counter-example'.

note: Follows the lemma-by-lemma structure but blurs several logical technical terms and adds a speculative note.
Faithful rendering of the karmic consequences of slandering the two Dharma-preaching monks, with the hells and their durations correct.

errors.english: If one thinks that the author's own intended position constitutes what is refuted in treatises, but not its auxiliary limbs
errors.why: The opponent's thought is that the word 'svayam iṣṭa' is included in the treatises for the purpose of exclusion, not as a component of the definition; the preceding 'whether present or absent it does not contradict the treatise' is part of that same thought.

errors.english: merely the crown nature [note: essential summit]
errors.why: In this logical context spyi bo'i ngo bo is best read as the general form (spyi), not 'crown'; the rendering and note are meaningless here.

note: A very difficult subcommentary on the svayam iṣṭa clause; the lemma structure is followed but several clauses are misconstrued.

errors.english: an endless jewel that cures fevers [note: an impossible or useless remedy presented as an example of an absurd goal]
errors.why: mtha' yas is the serpent king Ananta: this is the stock example of the fever-curing jewel on a nāga's head, a desirable purpose whose object cannot be obtained, not an 'endless jewel' or a useless remedy.

fix.find: an endless jewel that cures fevers [note: an impossible or useless remedy presented as an example of an absurd goal]
fix.replace: the fever-curing jewel of the serpent king Ananta [note: a desirable purpose whose object cannot be obtained]

errors.english: Why then must it state the purpose of the subject matter?
errors.why: The Tibetan is an assertion ('rather, it necessarily states the purpose of the subject matter'), supported by the Dharmottara quotation and the conclusion; the English turns it into a question.

note: Gets the general drift of the debate on the purpose of the opening statement but garbles the classic jewel example and some of the argument's links.

errors.english: "mind" as that which is understood by this
errors.why: The etymology is instrumental: buddhi is 'that by which [something] is understood', not the object understood.

fix.find: "mind" as that which is understood by this
fix.replace: "mind" as that by which something is understood

errors.english: a part of the ultimate thesis
errors.why: dam pa'i don is a slip for dam bca'i don (as in the next sentence): 'a part of the thesis' (pratijñārthaikadeśa); 'ultimate' is a conflation with paramārtha.

errors.english: the mere experience of the nature of the self
errors.why: bdag gi rang bzhin here means its own nature (cognition experiencing itself, reflexive awareness), not 'the self'.

note: Verses and argument on dream cognition and the universal 'understanding' are mostly tracked, but key logical phrases are misread.
